Sales Agents

External partners who sell on your behalf through the standalone Agent app. Their clients' identities stay private to them -- orders they submit show up here under their own name with an "Agent order" badge.

All agents

Supplier-funded promotions

Products a supplier has agreed to fund an extra push on. Agents see these on their Explore page as a bonus commission -- never who's funding it -- and choose whether to add them to their own cluster.

Commission claims

Supplier-funded bonus commission agents have requested payout for. Your own margin never appears here -- an agent collects that directly from their client, it's not money you owe them.

Mobile money providers

Lets agents pay for their orders straight from the Agent app via a real MTN/Airtel payment prompt to their phone, instead of you confirming cash by hand. Each provider needs its own merchant API credentials for this shop specifically -- sign up on MTN's / Airtel's developer portal to get sandbox keys before going live. Credentials are only ever readable by shop owners/admins.

MTN Mobile Money

MTN doesn't have a portal page for this -- enter your subscription key above and click this to create a sandbox API user/key and wire up the payment callback automatically. Switch Environment to Production once you have a production subscription key from MTN's go-live approval and this same button will attempt it there too (untested against a real MTN merchant account -- if it fails, ask MTN for the API user/key directly and paste them into the fields below instead).

Categories

Suggested in the Category and Sub-category fields when adding a product.

Units

Suggested in the Unit and Pack unit fields on price entries.

Attributes

Reusable attribute names with their usual values — e.g. Color: Red, Blue, Green. Suggested when building variants, and values auto-fill when the name matches.

Money in

Suggested in the Category field when logging Cash In, and used to group the income chart on the Cash Book page.

Money out

Suggested in the Category field when logging Cash Out, and used to group the expense chart on the Cash Book page.

Locations

Every place you deliver to. Chosen when a customer or an agent is added, and used to group orders going the same way on the Pending Delivery board — which only works while one place is spelled one way.

Agent terms

What share of your margin external sales agents get, and how long a product must sit in their cluster before it earns a bonus.

Default share of margin

A percentage of what you make on an item, not off its price — 50% gives an agent half your margin, 100% gives all of it and they pay exactly your cost. Below cost is not reachable, whatever is set here. Any product can override either one in its own edit form; this is the fallback when it does not.

Cluster bonus

How long a product must already have been in an agent's commission cluster before a sale of it earns the bonus. Stops an agent starring a high-bonus item right before checkout just to collect on it.

Order timing

If an order sits in one of these steps on the Order Tracking board longer than its limit, its card gets a blinking warning flag. Leave a step blank or 0 to turn its warning off.

Shop identity

What prints at the top of a receipt. Until now every printout carried the shop's name and nothing else — a receipt handed across the counter has to say where it came from and how to come back. Leave a field blank and its line simply does not print.

To print with no dialog, make a desktop shortcut to Chrome with --kiosk-printing after the program path, and open the app from it. Receipts then go straight to the default printer. Set the 80mm thermal printer as the Windows default first.
Paper: 80mm roll, 72mm printed. The receipt is only as long as its contents, so short sales use short paper.

Default markup rules

Added on top of a supplier's wholesale or retail price to suggest a selling price in Compare Prices. Leave a value blank or 0 to skip it. On a variable product this is the fallback whenever a variant sets no rule of its own.

Wholesale markup rule
Retail markup rule

Agent discount override

A share of your margin on this product, not a cut off its price: 50% gives an agent half of what you would have made, 100% gives all of it and they pay exactly your cost. They can never pay less than that. Leave blank to use the shop-wide default from Presets. Affects the standalone agent app only, never your own quotes.

Wholesale — share of margin (%)
Retail — share of margin (%)

Variants

Add an attribute like Colour or Size, list its values separated by commas, then generate the variants. Each is searched and priced on its own and can carry its own markup rule. Prices themselves are entered later in the Price Registry, one row per supplier.

Add price entry

  1. 1

    What you are pricing

    Pick the product, or one specific variant of it. Choosing a variable product itself lets you enter that supplier's whole price list in one go.

  2. 2

    How this supplier quotes it

    Leave Pack unit and Units per pack blank if it is only ever quoted by the single unit. Unit = Kg, Pack unit = Bag, Units per pack = 25 reads as “25 Kg / Bag”. This is asked before the prices because a breakpoint is read as wholesale or retail by comparing its quantity against the pack size.

    What this supplier calls it on their own quotes and invoices. Two suppliers rarely use the same code for the same item.
    Only needed to compare this against a RIVAL product. One supplier quotes a Box and another a Pack; without this, nothing can say which is cheaper per screw. Leave blank if you don't know — it is reported as unknown, never guessed.

    Leave Pack unit and Units per pack blank if this is only ever quoted by the single unit.

  3. 3

    Pricing

    At charge
    Prices per variant

    Fill in as many as this supplier actually quoted and leave the rest blank; come back the same way later. Switching supplier reloads this list with whatever that supplier already has on file.
